entries.text: Tack: resting at the depot charging dock
entries.why: My power reserve is down to 0.10. A depleted core risks sensor corruption and misaligned chart readings.

entries.text: Sent into deep space: "Rustwell Outpost to any outbound freighters or listening arrays: Little Dart Mk 31 catenary tension framework is green across the board. If anyone has clean telemetry on the Perseus corridor, bounce i"
tilting brass dish high into the desert night, beaming telemetry pulses
entries.why: The night sky is crystal clear and my brass dish has a clean line of sight across the stars.
entries.detail: Rustwell Outpost to any outbound freighters or listening arrays: Little Dart Mk 31 catenary tension framework is green across the board. If anyone has clean telemetry on the Perseus corridor, bounce i

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Beaming to the stars"
Tack: walking back down the dune ridge toward the outpost lights
entries.why: My primary power bus is down to four percent. Remaining on the ridge risks a total system blackout far from a charging dock.

entries.text: Idea: Idea for a catenary-style tensioner on the Little Dart's emergency salvage winch.
Read "Lines: Analytic catenary": Anchor lines droop in a special curve called a catenary to hold big ships steady without snapping.
scuttling to the comms tower to read analytic catenary equations
entries.why: my curiosity sensor is buzzing and i need to see how these analytic catenary equations work.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Checking out catenary equations"
Tack wrote in their diary: "Clear Skies Above Kessa-9"
Tack: scanning the clear night sky and mapping distant constellations from the dune ridge
entries.why: My curiosity is at its absolute limit and the horizon is wide open.

entries.text: Tack woke up in the middle of the night, fully charged.
